posts.cooked:
I know what the numbers in the unlock text mean.

They are recording turn numbers, including Villain and environment turns, with the first Villain turn being turn 0.

The list of "ALL TURNS" is the turns in which Sky-Scraper switched size.

This is proven in UXM266's log, which has 3 heroes.  He first switches in Sky Scraper's first turn (turn 3) and then waits until her third turn (turn 13) to switch again.  He switches again in the following Environment turn (turn 14) and then waits until SS's next turn (turn 18) before switching.  This matches his list.

 

THere are three turns where he switches more than once, and his Valid Turns are 3, so that is almost certainly the meaning of that.

 

So we know the thing she has to do is switch twice within the same turn.  We just need to figure out what the number of valid turns needs to be, if she can be incapped and whether the heroes can lose to finish off the unlock conditions.

 

Edit: We do have proof that 1 valid turn is not enough and 3 is.  We just need to try two valid turns.

Edit 2: I guess we also need tests against Mad Bomber Blade.

I unlocked against base Baron Blade in the Temple, per McB's original. And made a point of having Sky-Scraper go between all three forms in the same turn three times (no more, no less).

7) Anything else.

WIn a game against any variant of Baron Blade with Sky-Scraper on the team. In at least three turns, Sky-Scraper must switch between all three sizes, and Sky-Scraper must not be incapacitated when you win.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
I just got around to doing this.

At first I was a bit baffled as to how to do the tiny / normal / huge thing in one turn, but what worked regularly for me was Argent Adept with the Lyra ( Harmony / Rhythm ) with Alacritous Subdominant (one hero plays 1 card) and Inventive Preparation (one player other than you plays 1 card). Then it’s easy - depending on her starting state, play 2 cards that flip her to the other 2 sizes.

For environment Wagner Mars Base has the meteor storm. Once it’s up you can wait forever to draw the correct cards and play them. Of course you have to flip Baron Blade first, since his front side has a timer.

If you include Parse on the team, you can build up enough Critical Multiplier bonuses that you can eliminate the Baron the turn you take down the meteor storm.
